clue.text: Illusion of sticky situation surrounding a head of government

indicators.note: the sticky-situation word wraps around what follows it in the clue

parts.note: a mire is a bog, or figuratively a mess one is stuck in

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of government

explanation.surface: A political leader caught in a scandal finds the escape route was never real.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert vision of water that is not there is the classic optical illusion.

clue.text: Gallons put on board before ship's departure

indicators.note: the gallons are taken aboard, set inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old poetic word meaning before
SS stands for steamship, a prefix in ship names

explanation.surface: Fuel is loaded before a vessel sets sail.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out or the act of leaving, a formal synonym for exit.

clue.text: Cutting from heather, a keen gardener's requirement

indicators.note: Cutting from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A keen gardener takes a cutting from the heather bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed garden tool for gathering leaves and levelling soil is a basic piece of a gardener's kit.

clue.text: Last of a cigarette, in true denial

indicators.note: the cigarette end sits inside the word for true

parts.note: real means genuine or true
the stub left after smoking is the butt

explanation.surface: A smoker swears they never touched the final cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a contradiction or refutation of a claim, a formal denial of it.

clue.text: Say you'll diet about this time of year

indicators.note: Say tells us to speak the phrase and listen to how it comes out

parts.note: spoken quickly these two words run together into the festive season's name

explanation.surface: Someone warns a friend that a diet will follow the seasonal overindulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmastide is the season the clue points to, with 'this time of year' meaning the festive period.

clue.text: Outrageous figures clad outrageously

indicators.note: an outrageous treatment of the letters of figures clad scrambles them

explanation.surface: Bodies dressed in a scandalous way cause outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the anagram signal share a root: 'Outrageous' defines, 'outrageously' rearranges FIGURES CLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameful and shocking behaviour is called scandalous, the same sense as outrageous.

clue.text: Intends to indicate wealth

definitions.meaning: to have in mind as a purpose, as in 'she plans to go'
money or resources, as in 'a person of independent fortune'

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to show off their riches.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is to have a purpose; as a plural noun it is one's financial resources.

clue.text: Pastry chef oddly featured in article in newspaper

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

indicators.note: oddly keeps the first and third letters of chef

explanation.surface: A pastry cook gets written up in the food section.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist's written item in a paper is commonly called a piece.

clue.text: Entertain royal equerry, just wanting introduction

parts.note: regal means befitting a monarch, royal

indicators.note: only the introduction of equerry is wanted, its first letter

explanation.surface: A king's attendant needs only to be presented to keep the court amused.
explanation.walkthrough: An equerry is an officer attending a British royal.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to amuse them with stories or lavish hospitality.

clue.text: Pictures mostly universal church returning and promoting unity

indicators.note: returning reads the whole assembled string from back to front
mostly drops the final letter of the word for pictures

parts.note: the pictures is an informal name for the cinema
U is the British film rating for universal audiences
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Films and a worldwide church come back together for the sake of harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: CINEM + U + CE gives CINEMUCE, which 'returning' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical efforts seek unity among different Christian churches, the sense of fostering togetherness.

clue.text: Junior to avoid such a slip

parts.note: a junior is under someone in rank
to skirt an issue is to avoid it

explanation.surface: A junior employee is warned not to make that kind of blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like a mistake, but here it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a petticoat worn beneath a dress, the very garment this is.

clue.text: Got up, rejecting small eggs

indicators.note: rejecting throws the letter for small out of the word

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone gets out of bed and turns down a small breakfast of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish spawn, the mass of eggs in a female fish, is eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: See below part of mainframe

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie inside the word mainframe

explanation.surface: A reader is directed to a footnote on computer hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for underneath, used in scholarly texts to refer the reader to a later passage.

clue.text: Long golf shot topped

indicators.note: topped cuts off the first letter, the top of a down light or the head of a word

parts.note: a pitch is a short lofted approach shot in golf

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a long shot but tops the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a description of the shot but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn or crave it, the sense of having an urge for it.

clue.text: Dejected, seeing hundred others killed in battle

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the rest means the others
the fallen are soldiers killed in war

explanation.surface: A survivor is downcast at seeing a hundred comrades dead on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen means sad and disappointed, a near synonym for downcast.

clue.text: Strictly accurate equipment letting in water, though no opening

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus

indicators.note: no opening removes the first letter of the leaky word

parts.note: porous material lets liquid pass through it

explanation.surface: Gear that leaks water is surprisingly said to be very precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigorous work is meticulous and exact, matching strictly accurate.

clue.text: South American rasta found outside old city in Florida

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: rasta is found placed around the letter for old

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Rastafarian from South America is spotted beyond an ancient town in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: Rasta is short for a Rastafarian, a follower of a Jamaican religious movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarasota is a Gulf Coast city in the US state of Florida.

clue.text: Ladies perhaps left, ducks!

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nought, so two ducks are two O shapes

explanation.surface: A friendly 'ducks!' as someone departs for the ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' is a British term of endearment; here it is two cricket ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladies is a women's public toilet, so an example of a lavatory, British slang loo.

clue.text: A greeting from Spain reciprocates one from across the seas?

indicators.note: reciprocates sends the pieces back the other way, reading them in reverse

parts.note: hola is Spanish for hello

explanation.surface: A hello from Spain is answered by a hello from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A + HOLA gives AHOLA, which 'reciprocates' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Hawaiian greeting, a salutation from islands far across the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Love may come after chamber music produced by this?

indicators.note: the love letter is placed after the chamber word

parts.note: a cell is a small room or chamber
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: Romance might follow a chamber concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber music' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowed string instrument makes music, so the definition describes the instrument by its sound.

clue.text: Block promotion

definitions.meaning: to stop up a hole, as with a stopper
a publicity mention for a product, as in a shameless advert

explanation.surface: A ban on publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stop up; as a noun it is an advertising mention.

clue.text: Smoother wave on the way

indicators.note: in an across answer the wave word is placed after the way word

parts.note: a road is a way
a roller is a long heavy sea wave

explanation.surface: A wave rolls in on the path ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: This heavy vehicle flattens and compacts road surfaces, making them smooth.

clue.text: Maitre d'hotel keeps blistering

indicators.note: keeps says the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A head waiter is kept on in sweltering heat.
explanation.walkthrough: A maitre d'hotel is a head waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blistering heat is scorching, extremely hot like glowing metal.

clue.text: Struggles to support the French taxes

indicators.note: in a down answer the struggling word sits beneath the French article, holding it up

parts.note: le is French for the
vies means competes or struggles

explanation.surface: People fight to prop up French tax demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Levies are duties or charges imposed by authority, the same as taxes.

clue.text: Hungry and keen to join group

parts.note: keen and sharp both mean having a fine edge
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Someone eager to become a member of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-set is an old term for being ravenous, keen of appetite.

clue.text: Those people will be tense initially, on edge

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of tense

parts.note: a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Others will be nervous and on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural object pronoun for those people.

clue.text: Opera singer left Italy for festival

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A soprano departs Italy for a music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Divali, or Diwali, is the Hindu festival of lights.

clue.text: True love's present result voted invalid?

indicators.note: an invalid vote is spoiled, so the letters of result voted are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: An election outcome is declared void.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, 'my true love sent to me two turtle doves' on the second day.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's gift for the second day is a pair of these birds from the singer's true love.
